notes.rhoWire: [owner] 2026-10-10 (D21), CRITERIA PAR1. || OWNER-SETTLED VALUE: rho_w = 0.25 - one cut costs as much as four wires. The owner settled this value, and the [owner] tag covers the value and the words below it, nothing else in this note. || OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim, and the whole of what he said here): "favor wires over cuts. cuts are harder and more error prone." || AGENT RATIONALE (written by an agent, not by the owner, and not endorsed by him; it is argument for the value above, not evidence of what he said). Because a wire bridge's failure modes - wrong length, lifted, shorting a neighbour - are VISIBLE ON THE BOARD and reversible with an iron, while a missed cut is visible nowhere: it is found by a circuit that does not work, after the board is built, and the labour difference does not close that gap. PIPELINE previously proposed rho_w = 3 by naming the cut's permanence and invisibility and then entering them on the CUT's side of the ledger, as a reason the gap is small; the invisibility IS the cost, so that was A SIGN ERROR IN THE ARGUMENT RATHER THAN A DIFFERENCE OF WEIGHT, and the correction is kept here with the value so the faulty reasoning is not re-derived. At 0.25 the optimiser will spend up to four wires to remove one cut and not five, and a wire-heavy board is a PERMITTED outcome rather than a symptom. What this number does not buy, which matters more than the value: it is not the mechanism that reduces the cut count - J enters the cost identity with a positive sign, so a split costs a cut and then needs a join a wire supplies, and anybody tuning rho_w in the hope of fewer cuts is tuning the wrong number. The levers that serve the goal are clustering and spending strips (PIPELINE 8.1.1).
notes.rhoSolder: [owner] 2026-10-12. THIS VALUE DEVIATES FROM CRITERIA PAR1, WHICH STATES rho_s = 1: the spec is left exactly as the owner wrote it and the departure is recorded in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-10-stripboard-pipeline.md under "Deviations from the specs, recorded rather than fixed in them". Ratifying or rejecting it is his. || OWNER-SETTLED FACT: a solder blob is not an artifact he builds - when a layout calls for one he runs a short wire in its place. The [owner] tag covers that fact and the words below it, and nothing else in this note: the VALUE 0.25 is an agent's reading of the fact and is argued for below. || OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim, 2026-10-12, and the whole of what he said here): "I don't like solder blobs. They are notoriously unreliable and they make troubleshooting maddening." and "A solder blob will turn into a wire on my bench". || AGENT RATIONALE (written by an agent, not by the owner, and not endorsed by him): THE PRICE FOLLOWS THE ARTIFACT THAT GETS BUILT. A blob on a layout is a wire on the bench, a wire is priced 0.25 by rhoWire, so 0.25 is what a blob costs him; at 1 the objective was pricing an artifact nobody makes, and was wrong by a factor of four against the one that replaces it. THE SUPERSEDED REASONING, KEPT SO IT IS NOT RE-DERIVED: rho_s = 1 stood as COST's objective had it - "one solder blob at one hole pair, comparable in effort to one cut, and VeroRoute derives where it goes without being asked" - and priced at a cut rather than at a wire "because the work is a deliberate join at a named hole pair, not a lead cut to length". The effort comparison was not wrong about blobs in general; it was about an artifact that does not reach this bench. WHY THE COUNT IS NOT MERGED INTO W AND THE PARAMETER DROPPED, which would have been one fewer number: OBJ1 makes F three line counts and states a distinction that survives his instruction - "B prices something the agent does not place, VeroRoute deriving the bridges itself; W is the opposite" - so B and W remain two separately reported facts about a board, V1's two-path check stays stated over the same three counts, and only the PRICE moves. WHY A BLOB IS NOT FORBIDDEN OUTRIGHT, which his statement might seem to license: B is only ever what AutoFillVero derives and no gesture in the move set can make one, so a refusal would be an eleventh hard constraint rejecting a board for a feature the fork produced - and an agent may not author a hard constraint (grade.ts refuses a set that is not exactly CRITERIA's ten). WHAT THIS COSTS, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: at rho_s = rho_w the objective can no longer tell a wire from a blob, so the asymmetric test that caught a swap of the two weights is gone - correctly, because under his instruction there is nothing left to swap. RANKING's third position still orders fewer blobs ahead at equal F, and score.solder still reports the count. WHAT IT MOVES IN THE MEASURED RECORD: one of the fifteen runs in docs/stripboard/pipeline-verification.md section 6.9 carries a SOLDER line at all (random seed 3, B = 1, F = 16 at C = 15, which becomes 15.25 at this weight); B = 0 on every other run, so the weight is inert on fourteen of fifteen and cheapening it is not what closes a net - the completeness key recorded beside it is.
notes.kappaBench: [owner] 2026-10-16, CRITERIA K2 and K3. || OWNER-SETTLED VALUE: kappa_bench is DELIBERATELY UNSET. null here means UNSET ON PURPOSE, not absent by accident: the key is REQUIRED and the loader refuses its absence by name, so "no clustering bound" is a recorded decision a reviewer can see rather than a line somebody forgot. That is tau's pattern and it is followed here deliberately - read tau's note beside this one. || OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim, 2026-10-16, after being shown the render of the materialised pultec-low-boost that the adoption gate had just refused at kappa = 0.25, and the whole of what he said here): "i prefer the loose layout. It's much easier to build. I don't see the problem" and "if the layout is electrically correct, let's keep it. It looks fine to me". THOSE TWO SENTENCES ARE THE AUTHORITY FOR THIS VALUE, and nothing below adds to them. || WHAT WAS WITHDRAWN, AND THE HONEST REASON (agent-written, like everything below this point): the previous value was kappa <= 0.05 with a four-condition ratchet under it. It is withdrawn NOT for having been too tight - that would be the gate becoming inconvenient, which is exactly the move its own note forbids - but because IT WAS AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION AN AGENT AUTHORED FOR AN ARTIFACT AGENTS PRODUCE. CLAUDE.md states the invariant without exception: "An agent may never author the acceptance criteria for the artifact it is producing." The superseded note admits as much in its own words - "OWNER'S WORDS: none recorded. Owner-settled; no verbatim instruction recorded for this value, and none is reconstructed here from context - the characterisations below, including the ratchet wording, are an agent's" - so the elaborate rationale and the ratchet under it were labelled an agent's reasoning and explicitly not endorsed by him. It was found the way this class of defect is always found: it refused a board he said he preferred. || THE FOUR MEASURED FIGURES, which are the decisive evidence and are carried here rather than cited: the four hand-laid boards in this repository measure kappa = 0.055, 0.181, 0.196 and 0.269. THE WITHDRAWN BOUND OF 0.05 SAT BELOW ALL FOUR OF THEM, so it would have refused every board the owner has actually built and uses - and the board it did refuse sits at 0.25, inside that same range. The superseded note carries three of those figures and then argues for refusing them anyway; that argument is the one he overruled. || NO NUMBER REPLACES IT, which is the decision and not an omission: replacing one agent-invented number with another agent-invented number is the same defect wearing a different value. || WHAT null MEANS HERE. A2 DOES NOT FIRE: no clustering target is met or missed, the admissibility verdict rests on A1, A3 and A4 (tools/stripboard/verdict.ts), and the report prints A2 by its own three-valued name - "not-evaluated" - so an ungraded condition cannot read as a target met. KAPPA IS STILL COMPUTED AND REPORTED ON EVERY RUN: tools/stripboard/targets.ts computes it, Score.clustering carries it, run.json records it in canonical.metrics, and A2's own detail line prints the measured figure whether a bound is set or not. Unsetting the bound removed the GRADING and never the MEASUREMENT, and that is the whole point - a real value, if one is ever set, should be set from evidence this pipeline produced rather than from an agent's taste. SETTING ONE IS A DELIBERATE EDIT carrying the run that justifies it, a test beside it, and this note kept rather than overwritten. || K3'S RATCHET IS WITHDRAWN WITH THE BOUND, and why matters more than the fact: its four conditions are agent-authored - the superseded note says so over its own signature - and they were written to make an agent's number hard to move, which includes hard for the owner to move. A procedure an agent writes to protect an agent's criterion from the person the criterion is for is the invariant failing twice rather than once, so it does not survive as a constraint on re-setting this value. ONE CLAUSE OF K3 DOES SURVIVE, because it is sound whoever wrote it: the previous value and its reason are KEPT rather than overwritten, and the union of old and new is the record. The block below is that union. || PREVIOUS VALUES: 0.05, in force from 2026-10-10 until the ruling quoted above withdrew it on 2026-10-16. ITS WHOLE NOTE AS IT STOOD, VERBATIM AND UNEDITED, so the argument for it can be read and argued with rather than taken on trust - note that it opens by claiming the [owner] tag for a value for which it then records no words of his: [owner] 2026-10-10 (D23), CRITERIA K2 and K3. || OWNER-SETTLED VALUE: kappa <= 0.05, and its movement is ratcheted (K3). The owner settled the number and settled that it loosens only on evidence. || OWNER'S WORDS: none recorded. Owner-settled; no verbatim instruction recorded for this value, and none is reconstructed here from context - the characterisations below, including the ratchet wording, are an agent's. || AGENT RATIONALE (written by an agent, not by the owner, and not endorsed by him): kappa <= 0.05 is THE HARD END OF A RATCHET: start at a harder bound and back off gradually, only if it proves impracticable. It sits just under low-boost's measured 1/18 = 0.055, the best result any hand in this repository has reached, and IT IS NOT THE MEASURED VALUE OF ANY ARTIFACT AND DOES NOT CLAIM TO BE. Because a bound set where no artifact has ever reached yields nothing when it fails - set it at 0 and every run fails, saying only that 0 was not reached - while a bound just past the best demonstrated result makes a failure informative: something stopped the pipeline short of a thing a person has done, and the verdict has to name what. THE FIGURES THE BOUND IS UNINTELLIGIBLE WITHOUT, carried here rather than cited, so nobody can re-derive a loose bound without seeing them: the other three hand-laid boards sit at kappa = 0.181, 0.196 and 0.269 and ALL THREE PASS make check (PIPELINE 3.5, from RE-MEASURE), so kappa <= 0.06 would have refused three layouts that are built and in service. The obvious repair is to loosen the bound to admit them, and that is NOT the decision: those three are the cost of NOT minimising cuts rather than of trying and failing, and a gate calibrated on the former licenses the latter. The first runs are expected to fail this bound and that is the intent, so a failure is reported as REP2 requires and must not read as a malfunction. IT MOVES ONLY BY RATCHET (K3), four conditions, all required: (1) a run that demonstrably could not reach it, in the run directory, with its bound field and its evidence; (2) the binding constraint named FROM THE CONSTRAINT SIDE - maxSpanHoles forbidding the reach or minSpanHoles forbidding the compression, with the board and the net pair, or a packing infeasibility - because "the search did not get there" is NOT an admissible cause; (3) a deliberate edit to this file, the evidence in this note, a test beside it, and the previous value and its reason KEPT rather than overwritten, the union being the record; (4) never a silent widening, and never a widening because the gate became inconvenient. PREVIOUS VALUES: none. At schema 1 this is the first value this file has carried, and the three measured figures above are the values it was NOT fitted to.
notes.tau: [owner] 2026-10-10, CRITERIA K4. || OWNER-SETTLED VALUE: tau is DELIBERATELY UNSET. null here means UNSET ON PURPOSE, not absent by accident: the key is REQUIRED and the loader refuses its absence, so "no tolerance" is a recorded decision that a reviewer can see rather than a line somebody forgot. The owner was asked to choose a tolerance and declined; he has set no value and no default. || OWNER'S WORDS: none recorded. Owner-settled (as a refusal to set a number); no verbatim instruction recorded, and none is reconstructed here from context - the account below of WHY he declined is an agent's reading, not his statement. || AGENT RATIONALE (written by an agent, not by the owner, and not endorsed by him): he declined on grounds that were correct: the question was put to him with the wrong floor. He was offered "close 95% of the gap from 65 cuts to 19" on mid, where 19 is C_floor evaluated at mid's CURRENT S_occ of four strips - the floor for keeping every part crammed into the four rows --import used - while the floor against the board he actually owns is max(0, N - R) = max(0, 23 - 34) = ZERO. A tolerance chosen against a floor wrong by nineteen cuts would have been a number with no meaning. THE 0.05 FORMERLY CARRIED FOR tau WAS PIPELINE'S PROPOSED DEFAULT AND IS WITHDRAWN: it is not the owner's value, and no proposed default is substituted for it here, because a number used silently is a worse failure than one used knowingly and this one has nobody behind it at all. WHILE tau IS null, Q2 AND A3 DO NOT FIRE: an outcome of "valid, below target" cannot be reported against an unset target, so a run that is valid reports VALID with its achieved F, its derived floor and the gap, and the admissibility verdict rests on A1, A2 and A4. The pipeline reports the gap rather than grading it, because what a real run achieves on a real board is the evidence a threshold should be set from and none exists yet - every cut count in this suite comes from --import's placement or from a hand layout, neither of which is this pipeline. Setting it is a deliberate edit carrying the run that justifies it, under K3's ratchet. Note the two 0.05s in this file's history are unrelated: kappaBench is a dimensionless clustering fraction, tau a fraction of the gap to a derived floor, and the coincidence of digits is recorded so nobody reads one as derived from the other.
notes.yieldFloor: [owner] 2026-10-10, CRITERIA Q4. || OWNER-SETTLED VALUE: k = 1, carried as A LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, written to be revised rather than defended. This is Q4's k: with g = F - C_floor the gap that provably remains, r the recent improvement per evaluation and e the evaluations spent, the search stops when g / r > k * e. The owner settled that the rule is a hypothesis to be refined by experience, and the words below are his. || OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim): "we won't figure it out completely by thinking really hard. We need a credible hypothesis for what might work that isn't obviously dumb that we continuously refine as we get more experience." || AGENT RATIONALE (written by an agent, not by the owner, and not endorsed by him): k = 1 is a dimensionless RATIO OF EFFORT TO EFFORT, which is the part that transfers between boards, and it is measured across at least one restart and never within a climb. WHY IT IS ONLY A HYPOTHESIS, stated so it can be shown wrong: g is OPTIMISTIC, because the derived floor ignores physical reach and mid's net graph wants a six-hole span where its B32529 capacitors reach four, so the rule projects against a larger gap than exists and biases toward searching too long - the safe direction, and a bias rather than a forecast; r is BURSTY, a climb going flat and then dropping sharply after a restart, so a rate measured inside a flat stretch is not the rate of the search; and NEITHER HAS BEEN MEASURED ON A REAL RUN OF THIS PIPELINE. What refines it: run.json records the full improvement trace - evaluations, F, and the restart boundaries - and because a stopping rule cannot be calibrated by runs that obeyed it, a periodic CONTROL RUN ignores Q4 and continues to the backstop, recording what the rule would have left on the table. That number, over several boards, is the evidence k moves on, under K3's ratchet. THE FIELD NAME IS INHERITED AND THE VALUE IS NOT WHAT THE NAME SAYS: "yieldFloor" carries the vocabulary of the marginal-yield constant Q4 REPLACED OUTRIGHT - PIPELINE's proposed one unit of F per 2,000 evaluations, a quantity of machine time dressed as a measure of returns, which had a constant tied to a unit of F and did not scale with a board's difficulty. The plan's Task 10 brief and its OB3 describe this parameter as PIPELINE's proposed default citing CRITERIA 10.2; CRITERIA Q4 and 10.2 as committed say the threshold was replaced by the owner on 2026-10-10 and is carried as a labelled hypothesis, and the criteria are the binding authority, so the provenance recorded here is [owner] plus hypothesis rather than [PIPELINE] plus proposed.
notes.evaluationCap: [model] CRITERIA Q5, whose provenance line tags Q1-Q3 and Q5 to COST 6.4 - so this is NOT AN OWNER DECISION, and CRITERIA section 10 records nothing about it waiting on him. Everything in this note is agent-written, which is what [model] means. (The record, kept rather than tidied away: Q5's row read "the owner's evaluation cap" until it was corrected on 2026-10-11 to state [model] outright, and this note asserted the same wrong attribution until the same date. Calling a derived number the owner's invites a later reader to treat it as a decision - and the reverse error, treating a decision as derived and improving it, is the one this file exists to prevent.) Q5 IS A BACKSTOP AND NOT A MEASURE: it exists to stop a bug looping forever, its only requirement is to be loose enough that a healthy run never reaches it, and A RUN THAT STOPS ON Q5 IS REPORTED AS A FAILURE RATHER THAN AS A RESULT - reaching it means either the search or Q4 is broken, and both are worth knowing. It is run-level and shared, restarts spending the same cap with the schedule's division of it recorded, so a restart cannot quietly grant itself more. 20000 IS A LABELLED DERIVATION FROM MEASURED TIMINGS and not a figure anybody settled: at PIPELINE 4.6's governing 11.71 ms per invocation and 5.5's four invocations per candidate evaluation (apply, autofill, check, dump) one evaluation is 46.84 ms, so 20,000 evaluations is about 15.6 minutes of machine time - an order of magnitude above the 2,000 evaluations PIPELINE sized as "roughly 94 s" and used as its threshold of returns, which leaves a healthy search room while bounding a looping bug to minutes rather than to a machine left running. THE ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE MARGIN IS A CHOICE AND NOT A MEASUREMENT: nobody has measured how many evaluations a healthy run of this pipeline spends, which is the figure that would settle it, and the first real runs produce it. It moves under K3's ratchet like every other number here. || RAISED TO 200000 ON 2026-10-15, BY THE OWNER, ON THE MEASUREMENT THIS NOTE ASKED FOR. The sentence above says the deciding figure is how many evaluations a healthy run spends and that nobody had measured it; Task 11's ladder is that measurement, and it is written up in docs/stripboard/pipeline-verification.md section 15. WHAT WAS MEASURED: both benchmark instances, both strategies, every seed, at five budgets an order of magnitude apart (200 / 2,000 / 20,000 / 200,000 / 2,000,000) - 70 runs, every reference net whole in all of them. THE OBJECTIVE FLATTENS AT 20,000 and no higher budget buys anything: F, and C/W/B cell for cell, are identical at 20,000, 200,000 and 2,000,000 on all fourteen run shapes. SO THE RAISE BUYS NO BETTER BOARD AND IS NOT MEANT TO - it fixes a MISLABELLING. At 20,000, five of fourteen runs stopped on Q5, including both seeded transistor-preamp-feedback runs, which are the runs that produce a board beating the owner's own hand layout. By the paragraph above, a Q5 stop IS REPORTED AS A FAILURE, so at its old value this parameter reported the search's best healthy result as a malfunction. At 200,000 no run reports Q5; at 2,000,000 none either. 200000 IS THE SMALLEST MEASURED RUNG THAT CLEARS IT, against a largest healthy run of 36,250 evaluations (steepest-descent; first-improvement reaches the same F for 26-51% fewer), so roughly 5x headroom. THE BACKSTOP IS STILL A BACKSTOP: at the measured 0.076 ms per evaluation the new cap bounds a looping bug to about 15 seconds, far tighter than the 15.6 minutes the superseded subprocess timing above implies, because the in-process search of this plan's Task 10 replaced the four-invocation evaluation that arithmetic was built on. THE ALTERNATIVE PUT TO HIM AND NOT CHOSEN: 2000000, same correctness and more headroom for a Pultec section, which is larger than either circuit measured, at about 2.5 minutes for a looping bug. He chose the recommendation. WHAT IS STILL NOT MEASURED, stated so the next reader does not mistake this for settled: no Pultec section has been run at any budget, and 36,250 is a figure from an 11-net circuit.
notes.signatureRun: [external] the sibling repository's failure-signature termination, adopted on the owner's agreement 2026-10-10, CRITERIA Q6 - INHERITED, NOT DERIVED, and carrying the same hypothesis discipline as Q4's k. The value is external and the reasoning below is agent-written; the owner agreed to adopt it and no verbatim instruction of his is recorded. Three consecutive results sharing a failure signature - the failing check names, the floating parts, the CUT_CONFLICT positions - stop the run, compared WITHIN AND ACROSS restarts, because three sharing a signature across two seeds is stronger evidence than three within one. It reports the cause and does not retry, a repeated failure being a systematic cause to fix rather than a candidate to skip. Three is the sibling repository's number taken from a different problem - PCB placement, not strips - so it is a plausible starting value and nothing stronger, and nobody has measured how often this pipeline produces three identical signatures for a reason other than a genuine systematic cause. TWO WAYS IT COULD BE WRONG, and the run record distinguishes them: TOO TWITCHY, three restarts happening to fail on the same constraint by chance where a fourth would have succeeded, visible as a Q6 stop whose control run goes on to find an admissible layout; TOO PATIENT, a board that genuinely cannot be done under its constraints grinding through many restarts before three line up, visible as a long run whose signatures were identical well before it stopped. Both are read from the signature sequence run.json already records, so no extra instrumentation is needed, and the number moves on that evidence under K3's ratchet.
notes.seeds: [external] PIPELINE R7 and E2, CRITERIA Q3. The value is external and the reasoning below is agent-written. --seeds 0 1 2 3 4 is the seed list the sibling repository's optimiser already uses, with the seed recorded per candidate, so it costs no new numeric parameter and E2's seeded restarts reuse it: a restart takes a different low-bandwidth ordering of the net graph and climbs again, keeping the best candidate across all climbs. THE RESTART SCHEDULE IS DERIVED FROM THIS LIST ALONE - which seeds, in which order, with which share of the run-level cap - never from elapsed time or remaining wall clock, and Q3 fires only when the list is spent, which is why a single no-accepted-move round is a restart trigger rather than a stop. Reproducibility depends on it (PIPELINE V6): the same seed list and the same inputs must reproduce the candidates. Distinct and non-negative is enforced by the loader rather than assumed, because a repeated seed is a repeated climb from the same ordering that spends the cap while reading as another restart.
notes.worseAcceptance: [no default, and null IS the value] PIPELINE E3, CRITERIA PAR3. Everything in this note is agent-written. E3 is the bounded acceptance of a worse candidate - accept a positive change in F within a configured bound, from a recorded seeded PRNG - and it is the classical escape from a barrier the net-cluster move does not happen to span. It is OPTIONAL AND OFF UNLESS CONFIGURED. NOTHING IN COST, MOVE OR PIPELINE SUPPLIES A SCHEDULE AND NONE IS INVENTED HERE, so unconfigured means E3 DOES NOT RUN, stated in the report, never quietly approximated: a bound guessed here would be a search behaviour nobody reviewed, and refuse rather than guess is the rule. null is a value and not an absence - the key is required and the loader refuses its absence by name - and 0 is REFUSED rather than read as off, because a bound of 0 accepts nothing worse and that state already has a spelling, and two spellings of one state is the ambiguity this file exists to prevent.
notes.stockRows: [owner] 2026-10-10, CRITERIA HC6. || OWNER-SETTLED VALUE: 34 STRIPS, measured from his own stock. He counted the strips and 34 is recorded ON HIS INSTRUCTION TO TAKE THE CONSERVATIVE FIGURE (reported here, not quoted), so the number is deliberately one less than his count and is NOT a measurement error to be corrected upward. THIS FIGURE IS PROVISIONAL, like every dimension here: the principle is stated once, in CRITERIA 2 under "DIMENSIONS ARE ALWAYS PROVISIONAL", which is the authority for this value's status - a strip count is not settled for having gone unannotated. || OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim, 2026-10-12, the standing rule over every dimension): "I may, at any time, decide to change the dimensions of any board at any time. The dimensions are ALWAYS provisional" || OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim, 2026-10-10, on this value): he counted the strips as "about 35". || AGENT RATIONALE (written by an agent, not by the owner, and not endorsed by him): HC6 checks the OCCUPIED EXTENT - max - min + 1 over the dump's PIN rows - and not the canvas, because GRID is VeroRoute's drawing area and --import leaves it at a default, so a canvas larger than the stock says nothing about copper. Pin extent is a LOWER bound on physical extent, since a body overhangs its leads; BOUNDS (M1.1) replaces it with the exact figure and tightens the check. A board cut from a different piece declares its own size in boards/<board>/perfboard.json, which overrides this default - the per-board declaration is also the owner's, being a fact about a purchase rather than a judgement (PAR4).
notes.stockCols: [owner] 2026-10-10, confirmed and qualified by him 2026-10-12, CRITERIA HC6. || OWNER-SETTLED VALUE: 27 COLUMNS, counted on the board he usually uses, AND PROVISIONAL - like every dimension here. THE PRINCIPLE IS STATED ONCE, IN CRITERIA 2 UNDER "DIMENSIONS ARE ALWAYS PROVISIONAL", WHICH IS THE AUTHORITY FOR THIS VALUE'S STATUS and covers stockRows, stockCols and any per-board size a boards/<board>/perfboard.json declares; it is not repeated per number, because a caveat on each invites the reading that an unannotated dimension is settled, and none is. The instance here: 27 is his CURRENT stock with larger on order, so it is a default pending a purchase rather than a property of the method, and NO DIMENSION FOR THE WIDER STOCK IS RECORDED because he gave none - none is guessed, placeheld, or written here as a conditional threshold. || OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim, 2026-10-12, the standing rule over every dimension): "I may, at any time, decide to change the dimensions of any board at any time. The dimensions are ALWAYS provisional" || OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim, 2026-10-12, on this value): "yes, my current stock is 27 columns. I have larger stock on order, but until it arrives, that will be the default width" || OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim, 2026-10-10, on a different board rather than on the 27 figure): his reading of pt2399-core, which does not fit this bound - "It doesn't fit on my stock boards. I improvised to make it work." || AGENT RATIONALE (written by an agent, not by the owner, and not endorsed by him): THE LIVE CONSEQUENCE, recorded here because it is already biting: HC6 refuses a board that does not fit the stock, and every measured refusal is relative to THIS stock. pt2399-core is refused at 17 x 36 against 34 x 27 ON WIDTH ALONE - 36 columns against 27 - so at least one board in this repository is currently inadmissible because of a figure the owner expects to change. AN HC6 WIDTH REFUSAL MAY THEREFORE BE A PURCHASING FACT RATHER THAN A LAYOUT DEFECT, and a verdict reading it as the latter has concluded more than the stock supports. WHAT INHERITS THE PROVISIONALITY, which matters more than either number: anything DERIVED from a dimension. C_floor = max(0, N - R) takes R from the strip count, so the derived floor is a function of today's stock and NOT a property of the circuit, and Q4's remaining gap, A3's achieved objective and K1's S_occ = min(N, R) are all measured against it. WHAT IT DOES NOT TOUCH: the frozen fixtures. B1-frozen is stated against the exact dimensions its hand layout was built for and B2 hashes them, so NOBODY UPDATES A FROZEN FIXTURE TO TODAY'S STOCK - that destroys the benchmark. His own low-boost layout fits inside 34 x 27 at a pin extent of 8 x 26 - twenty-six strips to spare - which is the evidence the stock is adequate for a Pultec section once the parts are packed rather than strung out. The four unfinished Pultec boards fail this bound ON SHAPE RATHER THAN SIZE: three to five strips by thirty-odd columns is --import's ribbon, a description of the placer rather than a constraint on the circuit. And pt2399-core at 17 x 36 does not fit, which HC6 refusing it is CORRECT BEHAVIOUR rather than a gate that is wrong - the quoted reading above is the owner's. That case and kappa_bench = 0.06 look alike and are opposites, which is why each was checked against him rather than reasoned about.
